name: xero-bank-transactions-to-zapier-table

trigger.authentication_note: NONE — `get-app ScheduleCLIAPI` reports `auth_type: ""`, so Schedule by Zapier needs no connection. The Xero credential moved OFF the trigger and into the workflow body as the `xero_wf` connection alias, because the body now reads Xero itself.
trigger.params_note: `moh` (Time Offset) MUST be the STRING "00", not the integer 0, even though `list-trigger-input-fields` declares it `value_type: INTEGER`. Its real choices are the zero-padded strings "00"/"15"/"30"/"45" (`list-trigger-input-field-choices ScheduleCLIAPI everyHour moh`). Publishing with the integer 0 was REJECTED — `ZAPIER_VALIDATION_ERROR: '0' is not an allowed value for 'moh'` — which is worth knowing: a bad trigger param is documented elsewhere in this repo as failing SILENTLY at publish, but a value outside a SELECT's choice set is caught loudly. Do not rely on either behaviour; verify `triggers[0].status == "active"` after every publish.
trigger.trigger_note: SCHEDULE trigger — fires hourly at the top of the hour, weekends included. It replaced the Xero `bank_transaction` POLLING trigger on 2026-08-06 to stop this Zap consuming Xero API quota; see xero_api_usage. The Zapier-internal subscription URL is https://hooks.zapier.com/hooks/standard/20495893/ff5fac39f8f34e13b5aa34e69a4866ad/ — that is Zapier's own plumbing for the schedule subscription, NOT a catch URL for any external service to call.
trigger.why_not_polling: A durable trigger has no polling-interval field: the `--trigger` payload accepts only selected_api / action / authentication_id / params, verified across all 43 live triggers in the account. So the classic Zap's `polling_interval_override: 5` had nowhere to go at migration and this Zap silently began polling at the account default (~1 min). A schedule trigger costs Xero nothing and puts the interval back under our control — the Xero read moved into the body where WE decide the cadence.

connections_note: NEW as of 019fd4b2. The body now calls Xero (`_zap_raw_request` GET /BankTransactions), so the credential is bound as an alias rather than living on the trigger. Note the shape mismatch: reads return {"xero_wf":{"connection_id":…}} (snake_case) while the publish/update flags take {"xero_wf":{"connectionId":…}} (camelCase). `app_versions` is deliberately omitted — drive-invoice-to-xero also calls XeroCLIAPI via runAction with `app_versions: null`.

connectionless_apps.ZapierTables: read/write via sdk.listTableRecords / createTableRecords / updateTableRecords / deleteTableRecords — no connection, no task cost
connectionless_apps.ScheduleCLIAPI: the trigger — auth_type "", no connection, and it never touches Xero

xero_api_usage.before: ~1,440 calls/day. The `bank_transaction` polling trigger polled Xero at the account default interval, every day, whether or not anything had changed.
xero_api_usage.after: ~24-48 calls/day. One hourly fire reads 1 page of /BankTransactions (2-3 only if the window spans more than 100 transactions).
xero_api_usage.why_it_mattered: Xero rate-limits per TENANT: 60 calls/min and 5,000 calls/day. Five Xero polling triggers on tenant 62699a8c exhausted the daily limit on 2026-08-06 — confirmed from Xero's own response headers, `x-rate-limit-problem: day` with `x-daylimit-remaining: 0` and `x-minlimit-remaining: 60`, i.e. the per-minute budget was completely untouched, so it was NOT a burst, a concurrency problem or a retry storm. Every Xero Zap in the workspace was down for ~10 hours (retry-after 33519s) and drive-invoice-to-xero dropped two invoices.
xero_api_usage.pattern: A schedule trigger is the interval knob durable pollers do not have. Cost moves from 'polls per day' to 'fires per day', and the fire rate is ours to set.

version_pinning_note: @zapier/zapier-durable 0.11.0 was npm-latest at build time but only ~20h old; the runtime rejects dependencies younger than 24h at RUN time, not publish. Pinned to 0.10.1.

bank_transactions.name: Xero Bank Transactions
bank_transactions.role: Owned and written by this workflow.

fields.type: Type (labeled_string — a plain string is normalised to {value,label})
fields.currency_rate: CurrencyRate — NEW: the classic Zap never mapped f9, so this column was null on all 651 rows despite being populated on ~36% of transactions

bank_transactions.downstream: drive-invoice-to-xero reads this Table to decide whether an invoice has already been paid. A pause here is a silent production fault there — it produces duplicate draft bills with no error. Treat this workflow as load-bearing.

date_coercion_note: The `date` column is written as YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00Z. A bare YYYY-MM-DD is interpreted in the account's local timezone (Asia/Singapore) and lands 8 hours off, which shifts every date-window query run against this Table by a day at the boundaries.
description: Hourly schedule -> read Xero bank transactions dated in the [newest mirrored row - 7d, today] window -> find-or-create/refresh each row in the 'Xero Bank Transactions' Zapier Table, keyed on bank_transaction_id. Migration of the classic Zap 'Process New Reconciled Transactions', which created unconditionally. Adds: find-or-create, race-safe dedupe of concurrent creates (converge on the earliest ULID), refresh of an existing row when a mirrored field has actually changed, and the previously-unmapped currency_rate column. Since 019fd4b2 it is schedule-driven rather than Xero-poll-driven, which cut its Xero API cost ~97% and made it self-healing.
dedupe_note: NO separate state table is needed, and none was created. The mirror Table IS the dedupe state: each transaction is looked up by its own key (`bank_transaction_id`) to decide create-vs-update, and stray rows are deleted so the key stays unique. This is why bank_transaction was the cheapest poller to convert — an ALERTING Zap (xero-draft-bill-to-slack-alert, xero-draft-sales-invoice-to-slack-alert) writes nothing, so it depends entirely on Zapier's built-in polling dedupe and needs new state of its own before it can move to a schedule.

version_history.note: Xero POLLING trigger -> SCHEDULE trigger. Replaces XeroCLIAPI@2.20.5/bank_transaction with ScheduleCLIAPI@1.7.0/everyHour and moves the Xero read into the body: a bounded GET /BankTransactions over [newest mirrored row - OVERLAP_DAYS(7), today], hard-capped at MAX_PAGES(3) and MAX_TRANSACTIONS(200), warning loudly rather than truncating silently. Cuts Xero API cost from ~1,440 calls/day to ~24-48 — the reason for the change; see xero_api_usage. Binds the `xero_wf` connection for the first time (the body never called Xero before). The upsert, dedupe, snapshot and change-detection logic is unchanged. ALSO FIXES THREE KNOWN GAPS, all as a side effect of re-reading a window instead of consuming a dedupe store: (1) no_backfill_by_design — a failed run, or an hour the Zap spent disabled, is simply re-read next fire; (2) stale_columns — recent rows are re-read hourly, so the update path finally corrects the `reference` / `currency_rate` / `has_attachments` values Xero fills in AFTER creation; (3) it removes the staleness that made drive-invoice-to-xero raise duplicate draft bills. Validated before publish: tsc clean; determinism grep clean (the only Date.now() is inside ctx.step("today")); every sdk.* call reachable only from inside a ctx.step; run-durable in the real 0.10.1 runtime got through `today` (2026-08-06), `latest-mirrored-row` (newest row 2026-08-04) and built the correct window `Date>=DateTime(2026,7,28)` with NO DeterminismViolation, then failed at `fetch-bank-transactions` on the Xero daily-quota 429 that prompted this whole change. Verified after publish: triggers[0].status active, enabled true, 0 open drafts, deployed source byte-identical to the repo. NOT YET EXERCISED BY A SUCCESSFUL XERO READ — the daily quota does not reset until ~10:11 UTC 2026-08-06, so every fire before then fails harmlessly at the fetch step and self-heals on the next one.

replaces_classic_zap.title: Process New Reconciled Transactions
replaces_classic_zap.old_shape: XeroCLIAPI@2.20.5 bank_transaction trigger -> TableCLIAPI@1.25.0 create_record (unconditional), mapping f1-f8, f10, f11
known_issues_fixed: Created unconditionally, so a re-delivery duplicated the row — the Table holds 4 duplicate pairs across 651 distinct transactions.
No way to correct a row after Xero restated the transaction or an invoice was attached to it.
replaces_classic_zap.status: Its create step was PAUSED, which is why the Table fell ~5 days behind and drive-invoice-to-xero began raising duplicate draft bills. Turn the classic Zap off entirely — do not simply unpause it, or both it and this workflow will write the same rows.

known_gaps.no_backfill_by_design: RESOLVED in 019fd4b2 for anything going forward. This was true of the POLLING trigger: it primed its dedupe on first poll, so a gap stayed a gap and re-enabling never recovered it. The schedule trigger has no dedupe store — it re-reads [newest row - 7d, today] every fire — so a failed run or an hour spent disabled self-heals on the next fire, up to OVERLAP_DAYS(7) deep. HISTORICAL GAP STILL UNFILLED: the ~7 SPEND transactions missing from 2026-07-21..2026-07-26 (including Anthropic 2026-07-25 SGD 104.58) predate this change and sit outside any current window. Still accepted — they were reconciled against their receipts in Xero by hand and their invoices have already passed through the Drive Invoices folder. To recover them deliberately, temporarily raise OVERLAP_DAYS or run a one-off with a wider window.
known_gaps.stale_columns: LARGELY RESOLVED in 019fd4b2 for recent rows. Xero fills some values in AFTER a transaction is created — sampled over 93 transactions, 32 had a stale currency_rate, 26 a stale reference, 14 a stale has_attachments, 1 a renamed contact — and the update path only fires when a transaction is re-read. The polling trigger almost never re-delivered, so these persisted; the schedule window now re-reads everything within OVERLAP_DAYS(7) every hour, so a value Xero backfills within a week of creation is now picked up. Rows OLDER than the current window keep their stale values, which remains accepted: no consumer reads those columns (drive-invoice-to-xero matches on contact_name, type, currency_code, total and date, none of which drift).
known_gaps.restatement_of_old_transactions: NEW, and the one thing the schedule window is worse at in principle: a transaction restated MORE than OVERLAP_DAYS after its date falls outside every window and is never re-read. The polling trigger was no better — 'New Bank Transaction' fires on creation, not restatement — so this is not a regression, just a bound worth knowing. If it ever matters, switch the fetch to Xero's `If-Modified-Since` header, which selects on modification time rather than transaction date.
known_gaps.next_incident: The mechanic worth remembering has changed. It is no longer 'a pause is silent and the gap is permanent' — the window self-heals. It is now: this Zap makes ~24-48 Xero calls/day, and the tenant shares a 5,000/day ceiling with every other Xero Zap. If Xero throttling returns, check the whole tenant's poller inventory before blaming this Zap, and read Xero's `x-rate-limit-problem` / `x-daylimit-remaining` headers rather than guessing from the error text.
